For this narrow gate, the question is whether *sourcing* the PKGBUILD (top-level scope) executes dangerous code during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`.

Every line in the global scope is a plain variable assignment: `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `optdepends`, `options`, the `source*` arrays, and the `sha256sums*` arrays. There is no top-level command substitution (`$(...)` or backticks), no `eval`, no `curl`/`wget` piping to a shell, and no encoded/obfuscated payload anywhere in the sourced scope. The source URLs all reference the project's own upstream (github.com/allisonhere/tidemail), and checksums are present (not SKIP).

The only executable-looking logic — running the binary with a `man` argument inside `if`/`install` — lives inside `package()`, which is not executed during `--printsrcinfo` and is therefore out of scope for this gate (and is benign regardless: it merely generates a man page for its own app).
</details>

The use of GitHub releases and explicit checksums enhances supply-chain security by allowing verification of the integrity of the downloaded binaries. No dynamic or runtime behavior is defined in this file — it is purely declarative.
